entries.title: Sources can write a digest of the research
entries.body: A new Digest in Sources researches what the article cites and, where it can, who has cited it, then writes an overview and up to four sections: what it builds on, who has taken it up, what it may have missed, and citations worth checking. Its sentences link to the passages they discuss; quotations are checked against the search extracts or abstracts they came from. It runs only when you press it, on articles you added, and is offered once the Experimental features switch on your profile page is on.

entries.title: Ask a question beneath a summary
entries.body: On articles you added, the Brief and Fuller levels of Summary, and a Sources digest, have a box beneath them for asking about what you just read; each digest paragraph also has an Ask in chat button. Your question opens a chat that quotes the text it is about, and the box becomes a link back to that conversation. In Chat, these conversations link back to where they started, and you can filter the list to Summary.

entries.title: Article downloads include the Sources digest
entries.body: When you download an article's data, a saved Sources digest comes with it: its research questions, the searches it ran, the checked quotations and the written digest.

entries.title: The privacy page covers the Sources digest
entries.body: The privacy page has a new paragraph on what is sent, and to which services, when you run a Sources digest; its last-updated date is 31 October 2026. The help pages for Sources, Summary and Experimental features describe the digest and the new boxes for asking questions.

entries.title: A literature search no longer starts twice
entries.body: In Sources' Where it sits view and in Marginalia, a literature search could start a second time while a finished one, run from another tab, was still loading. It no longer does.
